title: Don't Blind Your VLA: Aligning Visual Representations for OOD Generalization
methods: representation-alignment regularizer (cosine loss to frozen C-RADIOv3 teacher)
question: Does action fine-tuning of a VLA degrade the vision-language representations inherited from its VLM, and can a lightweight alignment loss during SFT preserve them and improve OOD generalization?
key_findings: Naive SFT of OpenVLA lowers ImageNet-100 linear-probe accuracy on intermediate visual features: pretrained 79.88%, SFT 77.48%, Align 82.13%, C-RADIOv3 teacher 87.31% (Table 3).

VL-Think (8 board-selection domains in Simpler/WidowX): OpenVLA-7B is below its base PrismaticVLM in most domains, e.g. Arrow 0.26 vs 0.47, PublicInfo 0.24 vs 0.62, Weather 0.32 vs 0.62, Shape 0.40 vs 0.59; Color is the only domain at parity (0.69 vs 0.69) (Table 2).
Align only partly recovers VL-Think: Color 0.69->0.82, Shape 0.40->0.48, PublicInfo 0.24->0.30, but Arrow 0.26->0.24, Weather 0.32->0.27, Traffic 0.29->0.28 (Table 2).

OOD success on the RL4VLA-style Simpler benchmark improves with Align in most columns, e.g. Carrot 0.49->0.61, Instruct 0.74->0.83, Position 0.43->0.58 (Table 1); the paper states 'up to a 10% relative gain'.
Freezing the visual encoder during SFT collapses success to ~0.01-0.05 across all columns (Table 1).

Ablations: middle-layer alignment beats early (Semantic 0.61 vs 0.51, p<0.01) and late (0.54, p=0.03); Backbone2Enc beats Enc2Enc on Semantic (0.61 vs 0.55, p=0.01); C-RADIOv3 beats DINOv2/SigLIP/Theia; frozen MLP projector beats trainable ones; cosine loss with weight 0.2 best.

Qualitative: OpenVLA attention maps in layers ~14-24 are diffuse ('attention sink') vs object-centred Qwen2.5-VL; t-SNE of COCO object tokens shows overlapping classes for OpenVLA vs separated for PrismaticVLM/Qwen2.5-VL.

benchmarks: Simpler (WidowX-250S, ManiSkill3) OOD benchmark from RL4VLA (Liu et al. 2025): Semantic / Vision / Execution axes
evidence.scale: 1400 motion-planner demonstrations for SFT; each model variant evaluated over 128 randomized evaluation seeds per environment; appears to be one training run per configuration (training-seed variance not reported)
evidence.statistics: partial: mean +/- SD over 128 eval seeds; one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for ablations; no tests reported for the main Default vs Align comparison in Table 1; no training-seed replication
evidence.baselines: Default SFT (LoRA), Freeze (frozen visual encoder); VLM references InternVL3.5, Ovis2.5, Qwen2.5-VL, PrismaticVLM

causal_validation: No interpretability claim is causally tested inside the model. The intervention is a training-time regularizer, and its effect is measured behaviorally. Attention-sink and collapse claims rest on attention maps and t-SNE (the appendix itself says t-SNE plots are illustrative only).
closed_loop: Yes for the policy results: OOD success and VL-Think VLA success are closed-loop simulated rollouts. The VLM side of VL-Think is a static VQA prompt, not closed-loop.
limitations_stated: Compute constraints: study covers fine-tuning only, not full-scale pretraining.
Align leaves most VL-Think domains unchanged; authors hypothesize the small, low-diversity SFT set and limited LoRA expressivity cannot restore rare concepts.
Linear probing run on a reduced ImageNet-100 due to compute; t-SNE plots are illustrative only.
critique: Only one model (OpenVLA, discrete tokens) and only simulation; no flow/diffusion-head VLA, no real robot, so the 'VLA fine-tuning blinds the model' claim is narrower than the title suggests.

VL-Think compares a VLM answered via VQA prompt with a VLA scored on closed-loop placing; these are different measurement channels, so the VLM-VLA gap mixes knowledge loss with action-readout difficulty.
The claim of 'consistent improvements across all axes' is contradicted by its own Table 1: PosChangeTo is 0.23 Default vs 0.20 Align.
Near-zero success of the Freeze baseline is suspicious for a LoRA setup and suggests a configuration problem rather than evidence about frozen representations.
Attention-sink and representation-collapse claims are qualitative (cherry-pickable maps, t-SNE on 3 COCO classes); only the 2.4-point ImageNet-100 probe drop quantifies degradation.
Evaluation seeds are not training seeds; with one training run per configuration, the p-values reflect eval-episode variance only.
one_line: Fine-tuning OpenVLA on robot actions erodes some of its VLM's visual knowledge (lower probe accuracy, worse symbol grounding), and a cosine alignment loss to a frozen vision teacher on middle layers partly fixes it and improves simulated OOD success.
